problem: Native identity writes synced the temporary file and renamed it without syncing the containing directory. A returned success did not establish completion of that directory update.
implementation: Keep the existing64KiB limit and one fixed temporary sibling per identity file; no new persisted artifact.

Open and pin the actual Linux directory, sync it before mutation, open the temporary relative to that descriptor, sync/close the complete file, rename relative to the same descriptor, then sync it again.
Check that the named parent still selects the pinned directory; descriptor-relative cleanup cannot delete an unrelated replacement parent's temporary file.
Errors after successful rename or changed final directory selection return a classified uncertain commit. They do not assert that the previous identity remains selected.

Block live Tailscale state reads after an uncertain commit. Retain the last successful export snapshot. Force a full durable write before a retry can succeed, including equal-value and absent-deletion retries.

For uncertain saved configuration, latch refusal of authenticated control, token-free claiming, boot enrollment and further writes. Cancel pending owned installation/session admission and the DSP/calibration lifetime; preserve the selected file for explicit reload recovery.
An uncertain startup migration returns an error rather than clearing the refusal at load completion. Pre-rename failures retain the original selected identity and its authority.
